marie.label: Marie
marie.meaning: From Hebrew "Miryam"; disputed meaning — "lady", "one who raises up", or "star of the sea".
marie.text: The name of Jesus's mother, Marie was by far the most common female given name in France from the Middle Ages through the 19th century, often used as a first given name paired with a second one (Marie-Anne, Marie-Louise...). Its extreme frequency in the records makes it a poor identifier on its own for genealogical research.

jean.label: Jean
jean.text: Borne by both Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist, this was the most common male given name in France for centuries, alone or in compound forms (Jean-Baptiste, Jean-Pierre, Jean-Marie).

pierre.label: Pierre
pierre.text: The name Jesus gave the apostle Simon ("you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church"), very popular in France from the early Middle Ages to today.

jeanne.label: Jeanne
jeanne.meaning: Feminine form of Jean, "God is gracious".
jeanne.text: Popularised in particular by Joan of Arc (Jeanne d'Arc), this female name is common in French records from the 14th century onward, with several regional variants (Jehanne, Jeannette).

louis.label: Louis
louis.text: The name of the kings of France (notably Louis IX / Saint Louis), extremely common across all social classes from the 17th through the 20th century.
